    11	/-!
    12	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — the residue field of a closed point is the base field
    13	
    14	This file **discharges** the residue-degree fact `[κ(P) : k̄] = 1` for a prime divisor of
    15	an AJC curve over an algebraically closed base field.  It is the input that
    16	`Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean` §5–§7 and `Adelic/SectionBounds.lean` §4 both reduce to,
    17	and which those files leave open.
    18	
    19	## What changes relative to `GlobalGeneration.lean` §7
    20	
    21	`hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` (there) derives the approximation statement from
    22	**three stalk-level instance binders**, and its own docstring records — correctly — that
    23	none of them is constructed anywhere in AJC, so that it "trades one unproved fact for
    24	three unbuilt instances" and is a *reformulation, not a discharge*.
    25	
    26	This file builds all three, for a curve `C : Over (Spec k)`, and so closes the gap:
    27	
    28	1. `Algebra k 𝒪_P` — `stalkStructureHom` (`Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean`) already
    29	   supplies the ring map; what was missing is that it is **compatible with the
    30	   `Algebra k K(C)` of `Adelic/GateInstances.lean`**.  That is
    31	   `algebraMap_stalk_functionField`, proved by factoring both through `Γ(C,⊤)`:
    32	   `stalkStructureHom = constMap ≫ germ_⊤` (`stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ`, from
    33	   mathlib's `Hom.germ_stalkMap`), after which mathlib's
    34	   `functionField_isScalarTower` matches the two composites.
    35	2. `IsScalarTower k 𝒪_P K(C)` — a corollary of (1) (`isScalarTower_stalk_functionField`).
    36	3. `Module.Finite k κ_P` — **not needed at all** on this route, which is the substantive
    37	   simplification.  §7's argument goes through `IsAlgClosed.algebraMap_bijective_of_isIntegral`,
    38	   which needs the residue field to be *integral* over `k` and hence a finiteness input that
    39	   AJC does not have.  Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.residueFieldIsoBase` proves
    40	   `κ(x) ≅ k` for a closed point of a scheme **locally of finite type** over an
    41	   algebraically closed field, obtaining integrality from
    42	   `isFinite_iff_locallyOfFiniteType_of_jacobsonSpace` instead.  `LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom`
    43	   is a hypothesis a smooth curve satisfies, unlike a bare residue-finiteness gate.
    44	
    45	So the exchange is: one open fact **out**, and in its place a `LocallyOfFiniteType`
    46	hypothesis plus the closedness of the point — both genuinely available.
    47	
    48	## The closedness input
    49	
    50	`residueFieldIsoBase` needs `IsClosed {P.point}`.  For a prime divisor this is *not* an
    51	extra assumption: `Adelic/FiniteMapToP1.lean` proves
    52	`isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one`, and a prime divisor has `coheight = 1` by
    53	definition while the generic point has coheight `0` on a curve.  `isClosed_primeDivisor`
    54	below packages this, taking the one-dimensionality of the curve as the hypothesis
    55	`hdim` that the sibling file also uses.
    56	
    57	## Main declarations
    58	
    59	* `stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ`, `algebraMap_stalk_functionField`,
    60	  `isScalarTower_stalk_functionField` — the compatibility layer (item 1–2 above).
    61	* `bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom` — `k → 𝒪_P → κ(P)` is **bijective** at a
    62	  closed point, from mathlib's `residueFieldIsoBase`.
    63	* `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — `HasRationalResidues k P`, **discharged**:
    64	  every function regular at `P` agrees with a constant to first order.
    65	* `residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — `[κ(P):k] = 1`, the campaign's residue fact.
    66	* `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve` — the **unweighted** principal-degree-zero
    67	  statement, from the ledger, with the residue input now discharged rather than assumed.
    68	
    69	## A note on an instance diamond (read before adding imports here)
    70	
    71	With `Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean` imported, `open scoped AlgebraicGeometry`
    72	brings in `overStalkAlgebra C x : Algebra k 𝒪_{C,x}`.  At `x = genericPoint C.left` its
    73	target `𝒪_{C,generic}` *is* `K(C)` by definition, so it competes with
    74	`Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra` for `Algebra k K(C)` — and the two are **not**
    75	definitionally equal (machine-checked: `rfl` fails).  Everything below therefore opens
    76	only `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`, and constructs the stalk algebra as an explicit `letI`
    77	rather than by activating the scoped instance.  Activating it would silently re-pin
    78	`sectionSub`/`orderGeSub`/`residueDeg` to a different `k`-action than the rest of the
    79	lane uses.
    80	-/

    87	open scoped WithZero AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

    92	/-! ## §1. The stalk `k`-algebra and its compatibility with `K(C)` -/
    93	
    94	section StalkAlgebra
    95	
    96	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    97	
    98	/-- **The structure homomorphism into a stalk factors through the global sections.**
    99	`k → 𝒪_{C,x}` is `constMap C : k → Γ(C,⊤)` followed by the germ at `x`.
   100	
   101	Both sides are the stalk map of `C.hom` precomposed with `ΓSpecIso.inv`; mathlib's
   102	`Hom.germ_stalkMap` is exactly the statement that the germ commutes past a stalk map.
   103	This is the lemma that ties `Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean`'s stalk algebra to
   104	`Adelic/GateInstances.lean`'s function-field algebra, which is built from `constMap`. -/
   105	theorem stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   106	    (x : C.left) :
   107	    stalkStructureHom C.hom x
   108	      = Scheme.constMap C ≫ C.left.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial := by
   109	  rw [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.constMap, Category.assoc]
   110	  congr 1
   111	  exact C.hom.germ_stalkMap ⊤ x trivial
   112	
   113	/-- **The two `k`-algebra structures agree.**  The image of a constant `c : k` in `K(C)`
   114	is the same whether one goes `k → 𝒪_P → K(C)` (through `stalkStructureHom`) or directly
   115	`k → K(C)` (through `Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra`).
   116	
   117	This is what makes the stalk-level argument of §2 usable in the order language of the
   118	adelic lane, whose `algebraMap k K(X)` is the latter.  Proof: rewrite the stalk map as
   119	`constMap ≫ germ` (`stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ`), then both sides are
   120	`algebraMap Γ(C,⊤) K(C) ∘ constMap` — the first by mathlib's
   121	`functionField_isScalarTower`, the second by `Scheme.algebraMap_functionField_eq`. -/
   122	theorem algebraMap_stalk_functionField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   123	    [IsIntegral C.left] (x : C.left) (c : k) :
   124	    algebraMap (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) C.left.functionField
   125	        ((stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom c)
   126	      = algebraMap k C.left.functionField c := by
   127	  haveI : Nonempty (⊤ : C.left.Opens) := Scheme.nonempty_top_opens C.left
   128	  letI : Algebra ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) :=
   129	    C.left.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk (⟨x, trivial⟩ : (⊤ : C.left.Opens))
   130	  haveI : IsScalarTower ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk x)
   131	      C.left.functionField :=
   132	    functionField_isScalarTower C.left ⊤ ⟨x, trivial⟩
   133	  have h1 : (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom c
   134	      = algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk x)
   135	        ((Scheme.constMap C).hom c) := by
   136	    rw [stalkStructureHom_eq_constMap_germ C x]; rfl
   137	  rw [h1, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply]
   138	  rfl
   139	
   140	/-- **The tower `k → 𝒪_P → K(C)`** — binder (2) of `GlobalGeneration.lean` §7, now built.
   141	Immediate from `algebraMap_stalk_functionField`. -/
   142	theorem isScalarTower_stalk_functionField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   143	    [IsIntegral C.left] (x : C.left) :
   144	    letI : Algebra k (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra C.hom x
   145	    IsScalarTower k (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) C.left.functionField := by
   146	  letI : Algebra k (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra C.hom x
   147	  refine IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun c => ?_
   148	  exact (algebraMap_stalk_functionField C x c).symm
   149	
   150	end StalkAlgebra
   151	
   152	/-! ## §2. `κ(P) = k` at a closed point, over an algebraically closed base
   153	
   154	Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.residueFieldIsoBase` gives `κ(x) ≅ k` as a `CommRingCat`
   155	iso for a closed point of a scheme locally of finite type over an algebraically closed
   156	`k`.  What is needed here is the *ring-map* form: that the composite
   157	`k → 𝒪_x → κ(x)` — the map the order language sees — is bijective.  That follows once
   158	the composite is identified with the iso's inverse, which is `residue_stalkStructureHom_eq`
   159	below: an identity of `Spec`-morphisms, checked through `Spec.map_injective`. -/
   160	
   161	section ResidueBijective
   162	
   163	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
   164	
   165	/-- **A prime divisor of a curve is a closed point.**  On an irreducible scheme all of
   166	whose points have coheight `≤ 1` (the curve condition, supplied by
   167	`coheight_le_one_of_curve`), a point of coheight `1` is not the generic point — the
   168	generic point has coheight `0` — hence is closed by
   169	`isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one` (`Adelic/FiniteMapToP1.lean`).
   170	
   171	This is why the closedness input of `residueFieldIsoBase` costs nothing here: it is part
   172	of what `X.PrimeDivisor` already asserts. -/
   173	theorem isClosed_primeDivisor {X : Scheme.{u}} [IrreducibleSpace X]
   174	    (hdim : ∀ w : X, Order.coheight w ≤ 1) (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
   175	    IsClosed ({P.point} : Set X) := by
   176	  refine isClosed_singleton_of_coheight_le_one hdim ?_
   177	  intro hgen
   178	  -- the generic point is maximal in the specialisation order, so has coheight `0`
   179	  have hmax : IsMax (genericPoint X) := fun y hy => genericPoint_specializes y
   180	  have h0 : Order.coheight P.point = 0 := by
   181	    rw [hgen]; exact Order.IsMax.coheight_eq_zero hmax
   182	  rw [P.coheight] at h0
   183	  exact absurd h0 (by simp)
   184	
   185	/-- **The composite `k → 𝒪_x → κ(x)` is the inverse of mathlib's `residueFieldIsoBase`.**
   186	
   187	Both are morphisms `k ⟶ κ(x)` in `CommRingCat`; `Spec` is faithful, so it suffices to
   188	check the induced `Spec` morphisms agree, and there both sides unfold to
   189	`X.fromSpecResidueField x ≫ C.hom` — the left by `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField` plus
   190	`fromSpecStalk_comp_eq` (`Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean`), the right by mathlib's
   191	`SpecMap_residueFieldIsoBase_inv`. -/
   192	theorem residue_stalkStructureHom_eq [IsAlgClosed k]
   193	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom]
   194	    (x : C.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left)) :
   195	    stalkStructureHom C.hom x ≫ C.left.residue x
   196	      = (residueFieldIsoBase C.hom x hx).inv := by
   197	  apply Spec.map_injective
   198	  rw [SpecMap_residueFieldIsoBase_inv, Spec.map_comp, Scheme.fromSpecResidueField,
   199	    ← fromSpecStalk_comp_eq, Category.assoc]
   200	
   201	/-- **`k → κ(x)` is bijective at a closed point of a curve over an algebraically closed
   202	base.**  Immediate from `residue_stalkStructureHom_eq`: an iso of `CommRingCat` has
   203	bijective underlying ring map.
   204	
   205	This is the statement that replaces `GlobalScheme`'s three-binder route: no
   206	`Module.Finite k κ_P` gate is consumed, because mathlib obtains integrality of `κ(x)` over
   207	`k` from `LocallyOfFiniteType` through the Jacobson-space finiteness criterion. -/
   208	theorem bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom [IsAlgClosed k]
   209	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom]
   210	    (x : C.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left)) :
   211	    Function.Bijective
   212	      ((C.left.residue x).hom.comp (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom) := by
   213	  have h : (C.left.residue x).hom.comp (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom
   214	      = (residueFieldIsoBase C.hom x hx).inv.hom := by
   215	    rw [← residue_stalkStructureHom_eq C x hx]; rfl
   216	  rw [h]
   217	  exact (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective
   218	    (residueFieldIsoBase C.hom x hx).inv).mp inferInstance
   219	
   220	/-- **Every stalk element is a constant modulo the maximal ideal.**  The surjectivity half
   221	of `bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom`, restated as the approximation statement on
   222	the stalk: for `a ∈ 𝒪_x` there is `c : k` with `a − c ∈ 𝔪_x`. -/
   223	theorem exists_const_sub_mem_maximalIdeal [IsAlgClosed k]
   224	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom]
   225	    (x : C.left) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set C.left))
   226	    (a : C.left.presheaf.stalk x) :
   227	    ∃ c : k, a - (stalkStructureHom C.hom x).hom c ∈
   228	      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.left.presheaf.stalk x) := by
   229	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (bijective_residue_comp_stalkStructureHom C x hx).surjective
   230	    ((C.left.residue x).hom a)
   231	  rw [RingHom.comp_apply] at hc
   232	  refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
   233	  rw [← IsLocalRing.residue_eq_zero_iff]
   234	  change (C.left.residue x).hom _ = 0
   235	  rw [map_sub, hc, sub_self]
   236	
   237	end ResidueBijective
   238	
   239	/-! ## §3. `HasRationalResidues`, discharged
   240	
   241	The stalk statement of §2 is now translated into the order language of the adelic lane.
   242	The translation has two steps and both are already available:
   243	
   244	* `f` with `ord_P f ≥ 0` lifts to `a ∈ 𝒪_P` — `exists_stalk_lift_of_order_nonneg`
   245	  (`ChiLedger.lean` §N14b);
   246	* `a − c ∈ 𝔪_P` becomes `ord_P (f − c) ≥ 1` — `mem_orderGe_one_iff_mem_maximalIdeal`
   247	  (`GlobalGeneration.lean` §7), whose statement is phrased on `orderGe P 1` rather than on
   248	  the raw inequality precisely so that `f = c` is admitted (the project's `ord_P 0 = 0`
   249	  convention would make the inequality form false there).
   250	
   251	The `k`-action bookkeeping is `algebraMap_stalk_functionField` (§1): the constant produced
   252	on the stalk and the constant the order language expects are the same element of `K(C)`. -/
   253	
   254	section Discharge
   255	
   256	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
   257	
   258	/-- **`HasRationalResidues` holds at every prime divisor of a curve over an algebraically
   259	closed field** — the residue fact of the campaign, now a theorem on AJC's own curve
   260	hypotheses rather than on unbuilt stalk binders.
   261	
   262	Compare `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` (`GlobalGeneration.lean` §7), which proves the
   263	same conclusion but from `[Algebra k 𝒪_P]`, `[IsScalarTower k 𝒪_P K(X)]` and
   264	`[Module.Finite k κ_P]`, none of which AJC constructs.  Here the first two are built (§1)
   265	and the third is not needed (§2). -/
   266	theorem hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   267	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   268	    [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   269	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   270	    (P : C.left.PrimeDivisor) :
   271	    HasRationalResidues k P := by
   272	  intro f hf
   273	  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
   274	  · refine ⟨0, ?_⟩
   275	    rw [map_zero, sub_zero]
   276	    exact (orderGe P 1).zero_mem
   277	  -- lift `f` to the stalk
   278	  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := exists_stalk_lift_of_order_nonneg hf0
   279	    ((mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf)
   280	  -- `P.point` is a closed point of the curve, so `κ(P) = k`
   281	  have hclosed : IsClosed ({P.point} : Set C.left) :=
   282	    isClosed_primeDivisor (coheight_le_one_of_curve C) P
   283	  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := exists_const_sub_mem_maximalIdeal C P.point hclosed a
   284	  refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
   285	  have himg := (mem_orderGe_one_iff_mem_maximalIdeal P
   286	    (a - (stalkStructureHom C.hom P.point).hom c)).mpr hc
   287	  rw [map_sub, ha, algebraMap_stalk_functionField C P.point c] at himg
   288	  exact himg
   289	
   290	/-- **The residue degree is one** at every prime divisor of a curve over an algebraically
   291	closed base: `[κ(P) : k] = 1`.
   292	
   293	This is the fact that `SectionBounds.lean` §4 and `GlobalGeneration.lean` §5–§7 both reduce
   294	to and both leave open.  It closes item 1 of the two-item residue list in
   295	`SectionBounds.lean` §4. -/
   296	theorem residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   297	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   298	    [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   299	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   300	    (P : C.left.PrimeDivisor)
   301	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
   302	    residueDeg k P = 1 :=
   303	  (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues k P).mpr
   304	    (hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
   305	
   306	/-! ### The consequences, with the residue input no longer a hypothesis
   307	
   308	`GlobalGeneration.lean` §6 draws two conclusions from `HasRationalResidues` — uniform global
   309	generation with threshold `b + 1`, and the unweighted principal-degree-zero statement — but
   310	carries it as a hypothesis `hres`.  §3 above discharges `hres` on curve hypotheses, so both
   311	conclusions can be restated with **one** open input instead of two.
   312	
   313	Read the remaining hypothesis carefully: `hledger` is the closed χ-ledger, and it is *still*
   314	not a theorem in this project.  `Adelic/LedgerClosure.lean` proves it on the whole effective
   315	cone from the one-point bump (`chi_eq_of_bump_of_nonneg`) and states the remaining half
   316	exactly as an `iff` (`chi_eq_iff_step_of_bump`); the negative part needs an input the lane
   317	does not have.  So what follows is a genuine reduction from two open inputs to one, not a
   318	discharge of the leaf. -/
   319	
   320	/-- **The weighted degree is the geometric degree on a curve over an algebraically closed
   321	base.**  `deg_k = deg`, with the residue-degree-one input discharged rather than assumed.
   322	
   323	This is what makes the adelic lane's weighted statements into statements about the geometric
   324	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree` that the rest of the project uses. -/
   325	theorem degK_eq_degree_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   326	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   327	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   328	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   329	    [∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
   330	    (D : C.left.WeilDivisor) :
   331	    degK k D = Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree D :=
   332	  degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one k
   333	    (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
   334	
   335	/-- **Principal divisors have geometric degree zero on a curve over an algebraically closed
   336	base, given the closed ledger** — the adelic route to the open leaf
   337	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`, now resting on the **ledger alone**.
   338	
   339	Compare `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_hasRationalResidues` (`GlobalGeneration.lean` §6),
   340	which takes both the ledger *and* the approximation statement.  The second hypothesis is
   341	gone here.
   342	
   343	This is the sharpest honest form of the leaf reachable today.  It is deliberately **not**
   344	substituted into `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`, whose statement mentions no
   345	hypotheses: doing so would make a hypothesis-free theorem depend silently on the ledger. -/
   346	theorem degree_principal_eq_zero_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   347	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   348	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   349	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   350	    [∀ P : C.left.PrimeDivisor, Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)]
   351	    (U₀ U₁ : C.left.Opens)
   352	    (hledger : ∀ D : C.left.WeilDivisor,
   353	      chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
   354	    {g : C.left.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
   355	    Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 :=
   356	  degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one k U₀ U₁ hledger hg
   357	    (fun P _ => residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve C P)
   358	
   359	/-- **Uniform global generation with threshold `b + 1`**, with the residue input discharged.
   360	Above weighted degree `b`, `𝒪(D)` is generated by global sections at *every* prime divisor,
   361	the residue-degree bound being `r = 1` on a curve over an algebraically closed base.
   362	
   363	Still single-field, and still conditional on the ledger, the base vanishing and the peel —
   364	see the three-gap discussion in `BoundedVanishing.lean`. -/
   365	theorem exists_bound_forall_generatedAt_of_isAlgClosed_curve [IsAlgClosed k]
   366	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsIntegral C.left]
   367	    [IsNoetherian C.left] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left]
   368	    [LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]

462:

464: `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` (through
465: `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`, `SectionBounds.lean` §4) reduce to the

467: algebraically closed base every closed point has residue field `k̄`".  This section
468: replaces the remark by a **machine-checked equivalence** to a concrete, checkable
469: statement about rational functions:

471: `residueDeg k P = 1 ↔ every function of order ≥ 0 at `P` agrees with a constant to
472: first order at `P`.`

474: That is `residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues`.  It converts the remaining leaf from
475: a claim about residue fields — which in this substrate would require identifying
476: `localStepTgt k P 1` with `IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk P.point)`, an
477: identification this project does not have — into an approximation statement in the order
478: language the substrate already speaks.

481: an algebraically closed base.  Doing so needs the multiplicative structure of `κ(P)` (a

489: (`Adelic/ResidueField.lean`).  Note how it escapes the obstruction just described — it never

9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — global generation above the bound
10	
11	This file closes the **third** of the three gaps the vanishing lane kept apart
12	(`Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean`, module docstring): *global generation*.  Until now
13	that gap was recorded as "not addressed at all"; the statements below address it, and
14	the docstrings there and in `Adelic/SectionBounds.lean` are updated accordingly.
15	
16	## What global generation means here
17	
18	`𝒪(D)` is **generated by global sections at a prime divisor `P`** exactly when some
19	global section attains the pole bound at `P`:
20	
21	`∃ f ∈ Γ(⊤, 𝒪(D)), f ≠ 0 ∧ ord_P f = -D(P)`.
22	
23	Such an `f` differs from a local generator of `𝒪(D)` at `P` by a unit of the DVR
24	`𝒪_P`, so it generates the stalk.  This is `GeneratedAt` below.  The sharper
25	statement is that the *whole* residue field is reached — the evaluation map
26	
27	`Γ(⊤, 𝒪(D)) / Γ(⊤, 𝒪(D − P)) → κ(P)`
28	
29	is not merely nonzero but **onto** (`evalMap_surjective`).
30	
31	## The mechanism: two vanishings, not one
32	
33	## A note on the ledger hypothesis
34	
35	Inbox item I-0394 objects, correctly, that `hledger : ∀ D, χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` is much
36	stronger than a consumer usually needs — and, quantified over *all* divisors, silently
37	carries finiteness content, since `Module.finrank` of an infinite-dimensional space is `0`.
38	
39	The theorems here that need the ledger at *specific* divisors therefore take it **only
40	there**: `ell_sub_ell_sub_pointDivisor_eq`, `evalMap_surjective` and
41	`generatedAt_of_vanishing` take two named instances, `hledgerD` and `hledgerDP`, rather
42	than the universal binder.  That is exactly what their proofs use, and it means a caller
43	who can produce the ledger only on the effective cone
44	(`LedgerClosure.chi_eq_of_bump_of_nonneg`) can still use them.
45	
46	The `∃ b, ∀ D, …` threshold theorems of §4 keep the universal form, and that is not
47	laziness: their conclusion quantifies over *all* divisors above a numerical bound, so they
48	genuinely need the ledger at every such `D` — and at `D − P` for each, which is not a set
49	that can be named in advance.  Sharpening those means sharpening
50	`exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` upstream first.
51	
52	The evaluation map is *always* injective — that is `localStepMapₖ_injective`, the
53	elementary half of node N14, and it is what makes `ℓ(D) − ℓ(D−P) ≤ [κ(P):k]`.  It is
54	onto exactly when that inequality is an equality, and the ledger converts the
55	equality into a statement about `h¹`:
56	
57	`ℓ(D) − ℓ(D−P) = [κ(P):k] + h¹(D) − h¹(D−P)`.
58	
59	So surjectivity follows from `h¹(D) = 0` **and** `h¹(D−P) = 0`.  This is why global
60	generation is *strictly* more than bounded vanishing and why the threshold moves:
61	`deg_k (D − P) = deg_k D − [κ(P):k]`, so to put `D − P` above the vanishing bound `b`
62	one needs `deg_k D ≥ b + [κ(P):k]` — the bound raised by the residue degree *at that
63	point*.

81	   closed points are unbounded over a finite field) and is `r = 1` over an

/-! ### The N14 residue-finiteness gate is discharged too

`Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)` — "`[κ(P):k] < ∞`" — is carried as an instance binder
by roughly twenty statements across the adelic lane, and `ChiLedger.lean` §N14 describes it
as "the gated keystone input, not re-proved here".  It is now **provable** on curve
hypotheses, and cheaply, because `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve` above needs no
finiteness at all: approximation by constants says every class in the quotient is a
`k`-multiple of the class of `1`, so the quotient is spanned by a *single* vector.

This is why §3 is ordered the way it is.  Proving `residueDeg k P = 1` through
`residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues` would require the finiteness binder, since that
equivalence carries it; deriving finiteness from the approximation statement *first* removes
the binder from everything downstream, including `residueDeg_eq_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`
itself. -/

/-- **The residue field is finite-dimensional, from approximation by constants alone.**
If every function regular at `P` agrees with a constant to first order, then
`κ(P) = orderGe P 0 ⧸ orderGe P 1` is spanned by the class of `1`, hence finitely generated.

Stated on `HasRationalResidues` rather than on curve hypotheses so that it is reusable: this
is the general fact that the approximation statement is *strictly stronger* than the
finiteness gate N14 assumes.  The spanning computation is the one in the `←` branch of
`residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues`; here it is used for finiteness rather than for
the rank bound. -/
theorem finite_localStepTgt_one_of_hasRationalResidues
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X] [Algebra k X.functionField]
    [IsConstantField k X] (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
    (happrox : HasRationalResidues k P) :
    Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1) := by
  have hone : (1 : X.functionField) ∈ orderGeSub k P (1 - 1) := by
    rw [mem_orderGeSub]
    exact Or.inr (by rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one]; norm_num)
  -- every class is a `k`-multiple of the class of `1`
  have hspan : (⊤ : Submodule k (localStepTgt k P 1)) ≤
      Submodule.span k {Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
        (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1)) ⟨1, hone⟩} := by
    intro z _
    obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ z
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := happrox (g : X.functionField)
      (by
        have hg2 := g.2
        rw [mem_orderGeSub] at hg2
        exact orderGe_antitone (by norm_num) hg2)
    rw [Submodule.mem_span_singleton]
    refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
    rw [← Submodule.Quotient.mk_smul, Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap,
      Submodule.subtype_apply]
    have hval : ((c • ⟨1, hone⟩ - g : orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)) :
        X.functionField) = -(g - algebraMap k X.functionField c) := by
      change c • (1 : X.functionField) - (g : X.functionField) = _
      rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one]
      ring
    rw [mem_orderGeSub, hval]
    exact (orderGe P 1).neg_mem hc
  -- a module whose `⊤` sits inside a one-vector span is finitely generated
  have htop : (⊤ : Submodule k (localStepTgt k P 1))
      = Submodule.span k {Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
        (orderGeSub k P (1 - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P 1)) ⟨1, hone⟩} :=
    le_antisymm hspan le_top
  exact Module.Finite.of_fg_top (htop ▸ Submodule.fg_span_singleton _)
